name: Basketball explosion error
goalName: Unity gives errors while working on the basketball explosion script
goal: When I added the environment model to the scene, a large amount of errors showed up. I was accessing a script that had been destroyed. It was in the explosion method of the object, which confused me, as I did not understand how the object was destroyed before that.

approach.text:
Because the console gave me the error that I was accessing a script that has been destroyed, I looked at places where I destroy the gameobject (the script itself is not directly destroyed). The basketballs are destroyed when they reach a y-position below -20, and when the explosion particles are finished. Both the explosion method and the loop through all basketball objects use IEnumerators, it can take a couple of seconds from getting the list of basketballs to destroying the basketball in the explosion method.<<image 4.png>>The above script is in the GameManager.<<image 5.png>>The above script is in the Basketball. Because it takes a couple of seconds to reach "Destroy(gameObject)" in the Explode function, the basketball could already have fallen below the previously mentioned y-position. Before adding the environment, basketballs would fall below the y-position before the round ended. The basketball would be destroyed, but the IEnumerator continued, and tried to destroy the ball again, resulting in an error.

I thought of two solutions to deal with the problem. I could add a boolean to the basketball whether or not the explosion is happening, and disable the y-position check when it is. Or I could add two checks at the Explode method to verify if the object has been destroyed (by the y-position check). Because the latter option does not use an extra variable and is one less if-statement in the update method, this is the most resource saving method.

normalLearnings: I learned to brainstorm possible solutions before implementing the first one I could think of.
I learned to make decisions to save the most resources.
result: No more errors showed up after the fix.
validation: The errors were gone, indicating the solution works.
contribution: This helps for a more maintainable code. The errors did not break the game, but errors should not be ignored.
